title: Index and query tokenize Unicode text the same way: CamelCase splits on any letter case, text is NFC, matching is casefolded
goal: kbfacts splits identifiers with non-ASCII capitals (PobierzŁącze -> pobierz, łącze; GetEntityÜbersicht -> get, entity, übersicht), normalizes index text and query to NFC so a decomposed Könige is one word, and compares words casefolded so Straße meets strasse. No setting; ASCII text tokenizes exactly as before, the public eval shares and the collected test ids do not change.

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import kbfacts as k
t1, t2 = set(k.terms('PobierzŁącze')), set(k.terms('GetEntityÜbersicht'))
bad = [w for w in (k.stem('pobierz'), k.stem('łącze')) if w not in t1] + [w for w in (k.stem('entity'), k.stem('übersicht')) if w not in t2]
bad and sys.exit('identifier parts missing: %s (terms %s / %s)' % (bad, sorted(t1), sorted(t2)))

import sys, unicodedata as u
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import kbfacts as k
nfd = u.normalize('NFD', 'Könige')
a, b, ka, kb = k.terms(nfd), k.terms('Könige'), k.key_terms(nfd), k.key_terms('Könige')
(a == b and ka == kb) or sys.exit('decomposed and composed Könige differ: terms %s vs %s, key terms %s vs %s' % (a, b, ka, kb))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import kbfacts as k
a, b, ka, kb = k.terms('Straße'), k.terms('strasse'), k.key_terms('Straße'), k.key_terms('strasse')
(a == b and ka == kb) or sys.exit('Straße and strasse differ: terms %s vs %s, key terms %s vs %s' % (a, b, ka, kb))

gates.question: How does the CamelCase split recognise non-ASCII capitals, given the stdlib re has no Unicode property classes?
options: Scan with str.isupper/islower (stdlib only, one small function replacing the CAMEL regex use)
Spell out Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A/B capital ranges in the regex
gates.recommendation: Scan with str.isupper/islower (stdlib only, one small function replacing the CAMEL regex use)
gates.reason: because it covers every script with case and needs no range table to maintain
gates.answer: Scan with str.isupper/islower (stdlib only, one small function replacing the CAMEL regex use)

notes: Premise (run at plan time, commit 459853b lineage): CAMEL.findall('PobierzŁącze') -> ['Pobierz', 'cze']; CAMEL.findall('GetEntityÜbersicht') -> ['Get', 'Entity', 'bersicht']; WORD.findall of NFD 'Könige' -> ['Ko', 'nige'] while the NFC form -> ['Könige']; 'Straße'.lower()=='strasse' is False, .casefold() is True. All reproduce. Baseline: rag.py eval -> questions=774 passed=774 verdict_ok=774 found_ok=774. Readers beyond kbfacts: kf_index.py lower()s query words at many sites and its index cache is keyed on the CAMEL/WORD patterns; kf_route.py lower()s question words; every other caller of terms/key_terms inherits the change and needs no edit. re has no \p{Lu}: the split needs a scan by str.isupper/islower or an explicit class. Checks 3 (rag.py eval) and 4 (perfcheck ids) each passes before the work and pin behaviour that must stay unchanged (the public eval shares and the collected test ids); every other check fails before the work with a one-line reason, not a traceback. Checks 0 to 2 read the public kbfacts.terms/key_terms/stem, which the index and the query both use, so the index side is covered through the same functions.
